slot.brief: Two lines through the origin with given direction vectors; find the direction cosines of the (acute) angle bisector using the sum of unit vectors.

stem: Two lines through the origin have direction vectors $(1,0,0)$ and $(3,4,12)$. What are the direction cosines of the bisector of the acute angle between the directed rays?

verdicts.working: Normalize the directions: u=(1,0,0), v=(3,4,12)/13. The bisector of the acute angle points along u+v, proportional to (4,1,3), whose unit vector is (4,1,3)/√26.

working:
Unit directions: $(1,0,0)$ and $\left(\dfrac3{13},\dfrac4{13},\dfrac{12}{13}\right)$.
Their sum is proportional to $(4,1,3)$, whose magnitude is $\sqrt{26}$.
Direction cosines: $\left(\dfrac4{\sqrt{26}},\dfrac1{\sqrt{26}},\dfrac3{\sqrt{26}}\right)$.
